entries.name: mcp__github__actions_get
entries.description:
Get details about specific GitHub Actions resources.
Use this tool to get details about individual workflows, workflow runs, jobs, and artifacts by their unique IDs.

resource_id.description:
The unique identifier of the resource. This will vary based on the "method" provided, so ensure you provide the correct ID:
- Provide a workflow ID or workflow file name (e.g. ci.yaml) for 'get_workflow' method.
- Provide a workflow run ID for 'get_workflow_run', 'get_workflow_run_usage', and 'get_workflow_run_logs_url' methods.
- Provide an artifact ID for 'download_workflow_run_artifact' method.
- Provide a job ID for 'get_workflow_job' method.

entries.name: mcp__github__actions_list
entries.description:
Tools for listing GitHub Actions resources.
Use this tool to list workflows in a repository, or list workflow runs, jobs, and artifacts for a specific workflow or workflow run.

perPage.description: Results per page for pagination (default: 30, max: 100)

resource_id.description:
The unique identifier of the resource. This will vary based on the "method" provided, so ensure you provide the correct ID:
- Do not provide any resource ID for 'list_workflows' method.
- Provide a workflow ID or workflow file name (e.g. ci.yaml) for 'list_workflow_runs' method, or omit to list all workflow runs in the repository.
- Provide a workflow run ID for 'list_workflow_jobs' and 'list_workflow_run_artifacts' methods.

filter.description: Filters jobs by their completed_at timestamp

workflow_jobs_filter.description: Filters for workflow jobs. **ONLY** used when method is 'list_workflow_jobs'

actor.description: Filter to a specific GitHub user's workflow runs.

branch.description: Filter workflow runs to a specific Git branch. Use the name of the branch.

event.description: Filter workflow runs to a specific event type

status.description: Filter workflow runs to only runs with a specific status

workflow_runs_filter.description: Filters for workflow runs. **ONLY** used when method is 'list_workflow_runs'

entries.name: mcp__github__get_job_logs
entries.description:
Get logs for GitHub Actions workflow jobs.
Use this tool to retrieve logs for a specific job or all failed jobs in a workflow run.
For single job logs, provide job_id. For all failed jobs in a run, provide run_id with failed_only=true.

failed_only.description: When true, gets logs for all failed jobs in the workflow run specified by run_id. Requires run_id to be provided.

job_id.description: The unique identifier of the workflow job. Required when getting logs for a single job.

return_content.description: Returns actual log content instead of URLs

run_id.description: The unique identifier of the workflow run. Required when failed_only is true to get logs for all failed jobs in the run.

tail_lines.description: Number of lines to return from the end of the log

input.body:
Investigated both flagged workflows per the `ci-performance-evaluation` skill (steps 1–2: confirm the regression is real and attributable before touching anything). Conclusion: **no PR** — neither workflow has a fixable local regression.

### `Claudinite executor`: not a real regression — a measurement-mix artifact

The run-level duration this task measures spans `run_started_at` → `updated_at` for the whole run. But this workflow's one job is conditionally skipped (`if:` on the trigger label) — a run where the label doesn't match completes in ~1–2s with no work done at all, while a `workflow_dispatch` run does the real checkout/setup/execute cycle.

Reconstructing the same current/previous windows from the raw run ledger and splitting by conclusion:

| | all runs (what the report shows) | non-skipped ("real work") runs only |
|---|---|---|
| current window | n=19, median 64s | n=12, median **95.5s** |
| previous window | n=35, median 12s | n=17, median **98s** |

Once the near-instant skips are excluded, the actual work duration is unchanged (98s → 95.5s, if anything marginally faster). The event mix simply shifted — this window had proportionally more real dispatches relative to skipped label events (12/19 vs 17/35) — which drags the run-level median up even though nothing got slower. Nothing to fix; this is a property of measuring wall-clock across a workflow with a skip path, not a code regression.

### `Claudinite scheduler`: a real median increase, but not a local code inefficiency

This workflow has no skip path (`scheduler-run` always executes), so the median move is real: reconstructing from the run ledger, roughly 40s (previous) → 64.5s (current window), consistent with the regression the report flagged. Job-level step timings across several sampled runs (both windows) show two mechanisms, neither a bug in this repo's code:

1. **Sequential `drain` job overhead.** `drain` only runs when `scheduler-run` found ready work (`pickable == 'true'`) — and because it `needs: scheduler-run`, it runs as a *second, separate job* (its own checkout + setup-node + script, ~6–13s) appended serially to the run's wall time. A run that drains is inherently ~10s+ longer than one that doesn't, purely from job sequencing, independent of how fast either job's own work is. Whether drain fires depends on how much work the fleet has queued, not on anything this run changed.
2. **Growing scan cost.** The "Instantiate, ready and reclaim work items" step itself varies widely across sampled runs (37–88s) and trends with the repository's own accumulated issue/task history rather than any single change — consistent with "the suite grew because the repo grew."

Both mechanisms live in the vendored Claudinite engine (`.claudinite/shared/packs/claudinite-tasks/queue/{scheduler-run,drain-dispatch}.mjs`), which this repo never edits directly — a fix, if one is warranted, belongs in the canon. There is no lever in this repo's own (non-vendored) config that would change either mechanism without widening this task's scope.

Numbers are approximate reconstructions from the Actions run ledger (a 100-run page per workflow, which covers both comparison windows) rather than a byte-identical replay of the report's own query, since the live query window has moved on since the report was generated — but the directional finding (executor: artifact; scheduler: real but architectural/growth-driven) holds either way.

entries.description: Create a new or update an existing issue in a GitHub repository.

assignees.description: Usernames to assign to this issue

duplicate_of.description: Issue number that this issue is a duplicate of. Required when state_reason is 'duplicate'.

delete.description: Set to true to clear this field's current value on the issue. When false or omitted, this property is ignored. Cannot be true when 'value' or 'field_option_name' is provided.

field_name.description: Issue field name (case-insensitive). Must match a field returned by list_issue_fields for this repository or its organization.

field_option_name.description: Option name for single-select fields. Validated against the field's options before the API call. Cannot be combined with 'value' or 'delete: true'.

value.description: Value to set. Use for text, number, and date fields (date as YYYY-MM-DD). For single-select fields, prefer 'field_option_name' so the option is validated before the API call. Cannot be combined with 'field_option_name' or 'delete: true'.

issue_fields.description: Issue field values to set or clear. Each item requires 'field_name' and exactly one of 'value', 'field_option_name', or 'delete: true'.

labels.description: Labels to apply to this issue

method.description:
Write operation to perform on a single issue.
Options are:
- 'create' - creates a new issue.
- 'update' - updates an existing issue.

parent_issue_number.description: Issue number of the parent issue. Only used when method is 'create' and cannot be combined with issue_fields. The new issue is created and attached to this parent in the same operation.

parent_owner.description: Repository owner of the parent issue. Must be provided with parent_repo. Omit both to use owner and repo. Only used when method is 'create' and parent_issue_number is provided.

parent_repo.description: Repository name of the parent issue. Must be provided with parent_owner. Omit both to use owner and repo. Only used when method is 'create' and parent_issue_number is provided.

state_reason.description: Reason for the state change. Ignored unless state is changed.

type.description: Type of this issue. For updates, pass null to remove the current type. Only use if issue types are enabled for this repository. Use list_issue_types to get valid type values for this repository or its owner organization. If the repository doesn't support issue types, omit this parameter.
